thesis: Simulation hypotheses must be separated by their testability and cannot dissolve questions of existence or moral responsibility.
role: Uses constructed worlds to distinguish empirical equivalence from ontological sameness.

ideas.statement: Simulation arguments are conditional on implementation, observer counting and model assumptions.
Models identical on every accessible observation cannot be discriminated internally, even if their substrates differ.
An outside administrator shifts explanatory levels without explaining all laws or proving moral authority.
If a simulation supports experience, its suffering matters; creators’ control produces responsibility rather than moral infallibility.

evidenceAndExamples.statement: A programmed gravity reversal can be new internally while belonging to an unchanged complete rule.
A specified symmetry violation could be tested without identifying an ultimate creator.

objectionsAndQualifications.statement: An anomaly must be separated from its explanation; lattice tests concern specific implementations only.

audit.notes: Every unit read. Thought experiments distinguished from empirical evidence.
